rationale: Update the event-backpressure question with the local construction result: the two variants of the same probe disagree, so the freeze mechanism is not settled and the account must stay unresolved with the contradiction recorded.

investigations.hypothesis: detect_and_emit_events awaits event_tx.send for every observed transition and is awaited inside the run loop's tick arm, so once the bounded event channel is full the actor task parks inside the tick arm: no further tick() (leader election heartbeat, resend and flush timers), no incoming-message handling, and no Command reply (not even the documented append_notify Timeout, which drain_notifiers would have produced).
investigations.discriminator: Two runs of the same 3-node in-process cluster that differ only in whether an unread event receiver exists: (A) nobody reads events at all (only the receiver the handle itself holds from spawn_actor); (B) a per-node consumer task reads events until a flag is set and then keeps the receiver but stops reading. The hypothesis predicts both variants park the actor after event_capacity transitions; the construction observations contradict that for (B), so the decisive next information is whether the sender in (B) actually observes a full channel - i.e. the real capacity/state of the event channel (Sender::capacity / try_send from a probe) and whether events are still being produced at that moment, rather than a further variant of the freeze symptom.

interpretations.rationale: Current account. Settled by source: every transition the actor observes is published with an awaited send on a channel created once in spawn_actor as async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity) (handle.rs:295-323, capacity field handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 at handle.rs:74); detect_and_emit_events issues those sends (actor.rs:169-199) and is awaited from inside the tick arm of the single run select loop (actor.rs:665-711), so a Pending send there stops op.tick(), incoming handling, command handling and decided-subscriber pushes. subscribe_events hands out a clone of that same receiver (handle.rs:254-259), and append_notify's Timeout endpoint is produced by drain_notifiers on the same tick path (actor.rs:201-222, contract handle.rs:114-137), so a parked actor would also withhold that documented failure. NOT settled: whether an unread receiver actually parks the actor. Local construction (native feedback, not retained receipts; harness draft/assurance_generated.rs) produced two contradicting observations on the same cluster shape (3 nodes, in-process transport, event_capacity=1, tick_period=2ms): (A) with no consumer task at all, i.e. only the receiver the handle itself holds, no node reached a stable leader within 10s and every current_leader() poll timed out - consistent with the park; (B) with a per-node consumer task that reads events during a healthy phase (leader elected, entries decided, all commands answered) and then stops reading while keeping the receiver (instrumented: the task confirmed it had stopped reading), the cluster went on deciding all 24 further proposals and every node kept answering commands, and a later append_notify succeeded - inconsistent with the park. Because both variants leave an unread receiver on a bounded channel, (B) defeats the currently stated premise that 'unread receiver + capacity reached => sender stays Pending'. Possible explanations not yet distinguished: the tick arm's send may not be the blocking point in (B) (e.g. produces no further events, or the send resolves immediately because the channel is closed/space exists), or (A)'s no-progress has a different cause than the one claimed. Until the decisive channel-state observation is made, the freeze and its consequence stay unverified, so no defect is asserted. Counter-limitations to carry: a dropped receiver would unblock the actor (the send error is ignored), capacity only delays the parking, no snapshot source states that the actor loop must stay responsive to a full event channel (the finding would rest on the handle-method contract plus the deliberate try_send design of the sibling egress paths), and the event_capacity=1 configuration is an extreme point of a knob whose default is 1024.
limitations: Local construction observations (harness drafts run by the agent, not controller receipts) cannot support a formal conclusion; variant (B) also used an agent-defined tokio-backed AsyncRuntime implementation rather than the crate's TokioRuntime feature.
The parked-actor consequence for the rest of the cluster (lost quorum participation) has not been observed at all, only the node-local command/append_notify endpoints.
